This is the well-known royal-family Lakshmi Narayan Bari in the Ujjayanta Palace grounds, Agartala - the two-storied temple at the entrance of the palace compound (Palace Compound, B.K. Road / Lakshmi Narayan Bari Rd). Dedicated to the divine couple Lakshmi-Narayana; local sources say a Krishna idol was consecrated in the sanctum about 45 years ago by Krishnananda Sevayet, and a tamal tree planted by the sevayet stands in the premises (verify). The temple is a major venue of Janmashtami celebrations in Tripura. CONFLICT FLAG: one AI-generated travel blog claims the temple was 'consecrated in 1999'; this contradicts the documented Manikya founding (1909-1923) and is treated as unreliable.

name: Laxminarayan Temple
town_description: Agartala, the capital city of Tripura in West Tripura district, on the banks of the Haora river near the Bangladesh border, about 90 km east of Dhaka. It holds the Manikya royal seat - Ujjayanta Palace (now a museum) - and the cluster of royal-family temples in the palace compound (Lakshmi Narayan, Uma Maheshwar, Jagannath).

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala - within the city, a few km away (verify).
travel.railway: Agartala Railway Station - a few km away (verify).
travel.road: Central Agartala; located at the entrance of the Ujjayanta Palace grounds on Lakshmi Narayan Bari Rd.
